sc: Jaundice at 12 hours of age → Pathological: haemolysis until proved otherwise
Jaundice at 3 weeks, pale stools, dark urine → Biliary atresia
Thriving breastfed baby, jaundice from day 7 to week 8 → Breast milk jaundice: continue breastfeeding
f: Appears day 2–3, peaks day 3–4, unconjugated, term peak < 12 mg/dL, gone by 2 weeks (3 weeks preterm)
Onset < 24 h · rises > 5 mg/dL/day · conjugated > 1–2 mg/dL · lasts > 2 weeks · baby unwell
Haemolysis: ABO, Rh, G6PD, spherocytosis · sepsis · cephalhaematoma · hypothyroidism · conjugated: biliary atresia, hepatitis
Total + conjugated (split) bilirubin · blood groups of mother and baby · direct Coombs · Hb, film, retics · G6PD · TSH
Phototherapy (460–490 nm) above the line · exchange transfusion (2 × 85 ml/kg) if above exchange line or signs of encephalopathy · IVIG 0.5–1 g/kg in isoimmune
Kernicterus (basal ganglia): lethargy, high-pitched cry, arching → athetoid CP, deafness, upward gaze palsy
trap: Jaundice in the first 24 h is never physiological · conjugated jaundice is never normal: refer at once (Kasai before 60 days) · phototherapy in cholestasis → bronze baby
